title: Por or para?
why: You've known para since the basics; this lesson introduces por and puts the two prepositions side by side, because English often has just one word, “for.” Purpose, destination, deadline and opinion on one side; cause, means, route, exchange and times of day on the other: the lesson wraps up the unit on richer sentences before the subjunctive.

{"lessons": ["

Para: toward a goal, toward a destination

English often uses one word, “for,” where Spanish has two. Good news: you already know para (purpose and recipient). Remember its core idea: para looks forward, toward a goal, a destination, a deadline.

UseSpanishEnglish
purpose (+ infinitive)Estudio español para trabajar en Madrid.I'm studying Spanish (in order) to work in Madrid.
recipientEste regalo es para ti.This present is for you.
destinationMañana salgo para Sevilla. / el tren para ValenciaTomorrow I'm leaving for Seville. / the train to Valencia
deadlineEl informe es para el viernes.The report is due Friday.
opinionPara mí, es demasiado caro.For me (in my opinion), it's too expensive.
usefulness¿Para qué sirve esto?What's this for?
employerTrabajo para una empresa alemana.I work for a German company.

A simple test: if you can replace “for” or “to” with “in order to,” “headed for,” “by (a certain date)” or “in my opinion,” it's para. So “to” + verb meaning “in order to” is always para, never a.

Necesito el coche para ir al trabajo.I need the car to get to work.
Hago una tarta para el cumpleaños de Lucía.I'm making a cake for Lucía's birthday.
", "

Por: cause, route, means

Por looks back or through the middle: what causes the action, the route you take, the means you use, what you give in exchange.

UseSpanishEnglish
cause, reasonGracias por tu ayuda. / Cerrado por vacaciones.Thanks for your help. / Closed for vacation.
because ofLlegamos tarde por la lluvia.We arrived late because of the rain.
meansTe llamo por teléfono. / Te lo mando por correo.I'll call you on the phone. / I'll send it to you by email.
route, place you go throughEl autobús pasa por Córdoba. / Damos un paseo por el centro.The bus goes through Córdoba. / We take a walk around downtown.
exchange, priceCompré la bici por cien euros. / Cambio mi turno por el tuyo.I bought the bike for a hundred euros. / I'll swap my shift for yours.
time of daypor la mañana, por la tarde, por la nochein the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening / at night
frequencydos veces por semanatwice a week
instead of, for (someone's sake)Hoy trabajo yo por ti.Today I'll work for you (in your place).

Set expressions with por

por favor (please), por eso (that's why), por fin (finally), por ejemplo (for example), por supuesto (of course), por aquí (this way, around here), por qué / porque (why / because).

“Thanks for” is always gracias por: gracias por todo, gracias por venir. And “in the morning” is por la mañana (not “en”): mañana por la mañana = tomorrow morning.

", "

Traps for English speakers

Some sentences completely change meaning depending on the preposition, even when English says “for” in both. Compare:

With paraWith por
Lo hago para ti.
(I'm doing it for you: it's a gift for you.)		Lo hago por ti.
(I'm doing it for you: in your place, or because I care about you.)
Trabajo para una empresa.
(It's my employer.)		Trabajo por la mañana.
(That's when I work.)
Salgo para Madrid.
(Madrid is my destination.)		Paso por Madrid.
(I'm going through Madrid.)
El informe es para mañana.
(It's due tomorrow.)		Te llamo mañana por la mañana.
(Tomorrow morning.)
¿Para qué estudias español?
(What for? For what purpose?)		¿Por qué estudias español?
(Why? For what reason?)

When in doubt, ask yourself: am I looking toward the goal or destination (para)? Or toward the cause, the means, the route, the exchange (por)?

Price: no preposition, or por

To say what something costs, you don't need a preposition: La bici cuesta cien euros. To say how much you paid for it, use por: La compré por cien euros. “For a hundred euros” is never para.

Por fin he terminado el informe para el cliente. Se lo mando por correo esta tarde.I've finally finished the report for the client. I'll email it to him this afternoon.
